topIssues.title: Archive sweep: abandoned and dead-since-2024 repos
topIssues.author: jefr90
topIssues.body:
## Context

From the July 2026 review of the public repository inventory, covering the developer-facing repo surface under `github.com/ethereum-optimism`. Part of the **Interop public repo cleanup** epic (#1008). This task is scoped so it can be completed without protocol-team involvement: no protocol-side decision, review, or code change is a precondition.

Targets: the four repos listed below.

## Finding

The inventory flags these repos as abandoned or dead:

| Repo | Lang | Last push | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `superchainerc20-compatibility` | TS | 2025-04-11 | Empty README, no description. Presumed SuperchainERC20 / ERC-7802 compatibility checker; original purpose unclear. |
| `optimism-starter` | Solidity | 2024-04-17 | Single-chain boilerplate. |
| `scaffold-op` | TS | 2024-08-09 | Single-chain dApp boilerplate. |
| `optimism-mud-starter` | TS | 2024-04-03 | MUD-based starter kit. |

## Scope

For each repo:

1. Check for inbound links from `docs.optimism.io`, the docs repo, and README references across the org **before touching anything**. Reuse the inbound-link sweep from #1014 rather than repeating it.
2. Confirm there is no current owner.
3. Archive with a README notice pointing at the supported alternative.

For `superchainerc20-compatibility` specifically: first try to establish what it was for and whether the capability is still needed. If it is, log that need as a separate issue rather than losing it in the archive.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Inbound-link check documented per repo.
- [ ] Each repo either archived with a notice, or explicitly retained with a named owner and a stated reason.
- [ ] No broken docs links.
- [ ] Any still-needed capability captured in a follow-up issue.

## Open questions

- What is the supported alternative for each of the three starter/boilerplate repos?
- Can anyone establish the original purpose of `superchainerc20-compatibility` given the empty README?
- Who holds org admin rights to execute the archives?

**Note:** archiving requires org admin rights. If `gh` cannot archive these, the repos will be listed for manual action rather than failing silently.

topIssues.title: superchain-tokenlist: finish or archive
topIssues.author: jefr90
topIssues.body:
## Context

From the July 2026 review of the public repository inventory, covering the developer-facing repo surface under `github.com/ethereum-optimism`. Part of the **Interop public repo cleanup** epic (#1008). This task is scoped so it can be completed without protocol-team involvement: no protocol-side decision, review, or code change is a precondition.

Target repo: `ethereum-optimism/superchain-tokenlist`

## Finding

`superchain-tokenlist` was never finished. It was intended to define how tokens are registered and bridged across the interop set. The README still says work in progress / not ready for use, and there is currently no registration path for SuperchainERC20 tokens.

## Scope

Decide whether to:

- **Finish** the v3 schema + registry, or
- **Archive** it and name the alternative.

Keep the decision at the **registry/tooling layer**. Anything that would require a protocol-side decision about token canonicality across the interop set is out of scope here and should be split out.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decision documented, with a named owner.
- [ ] If finishing: a scoped milestone for the v3 schema + registry.
- [ ] If archiving: notice added to the repo, and the SuperchainERC20 registration gap logged as its own issue so the gap is not lost with the archive.

## Open questions

- Who owns this decision, given the repo has no active owner today?
- If we archive, what is the named alternative for token registration?
- Where does the registry/tooling layer end and the protocol decision begin? Is that boundary already written down anywhere?

topIssues.title: Starter examples: consolidate into a single examples repo
topIssues.author: jefr90
topIssues.body:
## Context

From the July 2026 review of the public repository inventory, covering the developer-facing repo surface under `github.com/ethereum-optimism`. Part of the **Interop public repo cleanup** epic (#1008). This task is scoped so it can be completed without protocol-team involvement: no protocol-side decision, review, or code change is a precondition.

Targets: the starter example repos listed in #1014.

## Finding

The interop examples are spread across several near-identical repos with uneven maintenance. `superchain-starter-pingpong` was last pushed **2025-02-19**. Consolidating into one repo is the target end state.

## Scope

- Pick the target repo.
- Migrate each example, preserving history where practical.
- Update docs links using the reference map from #1014.
- Archive the superseded repos with pointers to the new home.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One examples repo contains all interop examples.
- [ ] Every docs link identified in #1014 is updated.
- [ ] Old repos archived with redirect notices pointing at the new home.
- [ ] No broken links.

## Open questions

- Which repo is the consolidation target: an existing one, or a new repo?
- How much history preservation is worth the effort? Subtree merge vs. plain copy with a pointer to the original.
- Does archiving these repos require org admin rights, and who has them?

**Blocked by #1014.**

topIssues.title: Starter examples: audit docs references before any archiving
topIssues.author: jefr90
topIssues.body:
## Context

From the July 2026 review of the public repository inventory, covering the developer-facing repo surface under `github.com/ethereum-optimism`. Part of the **Interop public repo cleanup** epic (#1008). This task is scoped so it can be completed without protocol-team involvement: no protocol-side decision, review, or code change is a precondition.

Targets: the starter example repos listed below, plus `docs.optimism.io` and the docs repo.

## Finding

Published docs link to several of the starter example repos. Archiving any of them without a reference audit would break live documentation.

## Scope

Inventory every reference in `docs.optimism.io` and the docs repo to:

- `superchain-starter`
- `superchain-starter-superchainerc20`
- `superchain-starter-xchain-flash-loan-example`
- `superchain-starter-xchain-eth-multitransfer`
- `superchain-starter-pingpong`
- `superchainerc20-starter`

**No archiving happens in this issue.** This is a read-only audit that produces the input for #1015.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A reference map of doc page to repo, covering all six repos.
- [ ] The map is published somewhere #1015 can consume it.
- [ ] No repo is archived, modified, or redirected as part of this issue.

## Open questions

- Does the audit cover only `docs.optimism.io` and the docs repo, or also README cross-references across the org? #1017 needs the broader sweep, so it may be worth doing once here.
- Are there versioned or translated doc pages that need separate treatment?
- Should non-docs inbound links (blog posts, tutorials, third-party) be captured as a best-effort list?

**Blocks #1015.**

topIssues.title: supersim: upgrade to the latest released OP Stack version
topIssues.author: jefr90
topIssues.body:
## Context

From the July 2026 review of the public repository inventory, covering the developer-facing repo surface under `github.com/ethereum-optimism`. Part of the **Interop public repo cleanup** epic (#1008). This task is scoped so it can be completed without protocol-team involvement: no protocol-side decision, review, or code change is a precondition.

Target repo: `ethereum-optimism/supersim`

## Finding

`supersim` is the default local harness for testing interop apps without spinning up a devnet, but it lags the current OP Stack version.

## Scope

- Identify the version gap against the latest **released** OP Stack.
- Perform the upgrade.
- Verify L2 to L2 interop message passing and predeploys work against current released contracts.

**Constraint:** consume released versions only. Do not scope work that waits on unreleased protocol changes. If the upgrade surfaces a blocker that needs an unreleased change, split that out rather than parking this issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Version gap documented.
- [ ] `supersim` runs against the latest released OP Stack.
- [ ] L2 to L2 interop message passing verified against current released contracts.
- [ ] Predeploys verified against current released contracts.
- [ ] Release cut.

## Open questions

- Which released OP Stack version is the target, and is there an interop-relevant floor below it?
- Is there existing automated coverage for the interop flows, or does verification need to be built as part of this?
- Should the upgrade cadence be automated afterwards so this does not recur?
